claim.text: Knight Frank commentary published 7 October 2026 argues London office development activity is not keeping pace with occupier demand for the type of space now required, citing viability pressures and macroeconomic caution. Attributed view, not a measured indicator.
claim.headline: Knight Frank: development lagging occupier demand

claim.text: Morgan McKinley's London Employment Monitor reports professional job vacancies in London fell to 4,368 during the third quarter of 2026, down 6% from the previous quarter and 11% year-on-year.
claim.headline: London professional vacancies fall in Q3 2026

claim.text: The same monitor reports monthly London professional vacancies falling from 1,719 in July to 1,449 in August and 1,200 in September, a 30% decline across the quarter.
claim.headline: Monthly London vacancies fall through Q3

claim.text: Watch whether London professional vacancy counts stabilise after the autumn Budget, which the monitor says could delay discretionary hiring; a further September-style fall would weaken occupier expansion assumptions.
claim.headline: Follow-up: post-Budget hiring caution

claim.text: ONS reported a London resident employment rate of 73.9% and inactivity rate of 20.5% for ages 16 to 64, and unemployment of 6.8% for economically active residents aged 16 and over, for May-July 2026.
claim.headline: London resident employment 73.9%, unemployment 6.8%

claim.text: The Bank of England reported UK CPI inflation increased to 3.1% in August, and on 16 September 2026 the MPC voted 6-3 to maintain Bank Rate at 3.75%.
claim.headline: UK CPI 3.1%; Bank Rate held at 3.75%

claim.text: GLA analysis cites the most recent ONS release showing London real GVA grew 0.3% in 2023 against 0.4% for the UK; GLA Economics estimates real GVA rose 1.1% in 2024 and 1.9% in 2025.
claim.headline: GLA: London GVA 0.3% in 2023, estimates for 2024-25

claim.text: The 2023 GVA figure is an observed ONS release cited by the GLA, while the 2024 and 2025 figures are GLA estimates rather than official outturn; GLA commentary attributes recent involuntary worklessness to weaker labour demand.
claim.headline: GLA estimates are separate from observed ONS history

claim.text: The hybrid figure is Great Britain-wide, covers survey working adults rather than office-only workers, and its January-March 2025 window is stale context that cannot establish current London office attendance or floor-area requirements.
claim.headline: Hybrid data is GB-wide and dated

availability: No reviewed availability measurement was retrieved; reported vacancy and pipeline are distinct from marketed availability.
midtown_fringe: Only City Fringe vacancy history is retained; Midtown itself remains unmeasured and City Fringe is not Midtown.
wider_london: Only selected districts (Hammersmith, VNEB, Stratford, Lambeth) are covered; these samples do not represent all wider London.
